newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates ease amid good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates ease amid good liquidity.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady to lower on Thursday as good banking liquidity forced lenders to trim some prices on Zagreb's money market, dealers said.
"Supply is really strong today, and it overshot demand by 70 million kuna ($10.7 million). Some banks just don't know what to do with their surplus money," one dealer said.
She said demand was higher than on Wednesday, but "banks mostly took one-day and call money loans to last till Friday".
Some 450 million kuna will be injected into the banking sector on Friday, following central bank hard currency purchases on Wednesday.
Fresh loans totalled 23.4 million kuna on Thursday, half of which were call money borrowings, granted at a steady 7.0-percent rate. The same rate applied to a one-day loan.
Rates for one-month loans were cut to 11 and 12 percent from the usual 13 percent.

Banks had 66 million kuna in Lombard loans, unchanged from Wednesday night. All banks were positive and Wednesday's overnight trade totalled four million kuna, granted to one savings bank for maintenance of its mandatory reserve. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.517 Croatian Kuna)
